findings.title: An accessible message meets resistant hearing
findings.claim: In this pericope, the message made easy through the messenger's tongue serves both the audience promised affection and the contentious audience warned; ease becomes a communicative path whose reception or obstruction is visible.
findings.mechanism: The focus makes the tongue-language medium usable for two paired acts, glad tidings and warning. The immediately preceding promise of affection gives the good-news audience a local setting, while the earlier driven disbelievers and the adjective luddan frame warning as meeting resistance. The contrast between caused ease and lateral or obstructive branches of luddan lets the message's direction, not only its simplicity, color the reading.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees facilitation as making a message available across different responses: good news can meet an affectionate audience, while warning is directed into contention and may be obstructed.
findings.containment: The ordinary readings of ease, tongue-language, good news, warning, and contentious people remain intact. The lateral and holding-back branches are contextual images, not alternative lexical translations of luddan; the packet does not say that every warned person rejects the message or that the message causes the promised affection.

epistemic.reason: The central carrier and purpose clauses are explicit in the focus. The pericope adds a specific audience contrast; the lateral and obstruction relations are contextual extensions and remain bounded as such.

In 19:95 the root image of resurrection and the single arriving person return against that group address, while luddan marks the group's current interactional posture. Together they change qawm from an undifferentiated bloc into an address-scale grouping whose members remain individually answerable.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear a collective warning without treating the collective label as a permanent essence of each person.
findings.containment: The focus still addresses a contentious group. The contextual reading does not deny that grouping, and it does not claim that the later individual accounting cancels the group address.

epistemic.reason: The totality, arrival, resurrection, and individual-arrival coordinates match the supplied context, but their corrective force on the focus label is an attributed inference.

findings.mechanism: In 19:96, trust and fitting deeds precede the Merciful's making of affection; 19:97 immediately gives the messenger an accessible tongue and a purpose of glad tidings to the God-conscious. findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the announcement as participating in a social relation, while keeping the promised affection itself as the primary content.
findings.containment: The focus does not say that proclamation creates affection. The possibility that 19:96 names an independent divine gift and 19:97 only explains linguistic accessibility remains.

epistemic.reason: The exact adjacent context and focus-purpose contact is supplied, but the claim that proclamation mediates the affection is an attributed inference from a legacy_unbound HFT record.

findings.title: A warning within an audible interval
findings.claim: The focus's tongue and warning sit immediately before a question about former generations whom no one can sense or hear, down to their faintest sound; the message is made speakable while a people's own audible trace can disappear.
findings.mechanism: The focus gives the messenger an accessible tongue, a warning act, and a qawm as its audience. The next ayah names destruction, asks whether any are sensed or heard, and ends with a question about even a faint sound. That acoustic sequence contacts the focus's present speech and warning, changing the tongue from a convenience for current hearers into a voice within a finite interval of audibility.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader notices the contrast between a warning that can still be heard and former peoples whose trace has fallen below perception.
findings.containment: The focus retains its ordinary claim of facilitated proclamation. The alternative that 19:98 depicts destruction without contrasting human silence and revelatory transmission remains open.

epistemic.reason: The adjacent acoustic wording and all traced focus roots match the supplied surfaces, while the finite-interval interpretation is attributed to a legacy_unbound HFT record.

findings.title: Warning as a resisted oral dose
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the focus's warning can be felt as a protective oral dose pressed toward a resistant audience: the side-mouth image meets the messenger's tongue, the self-protecting audience, and a nearby scene of coercive driving.
findings.mechanism: The ludd branch has a supplied specialization for medicine administered from one side of the mouth. In the focus, that geometry contacts lisānika as an embodied speech organ, muttaqīn as a self-protecting audience, and tundhira as danger-notice; 19:86 adds the pressure of wrongdoers being driven toward Hell. Together these carriers change warning from abstract notice into a prophylactic oral delivery resisted at its point of reception.
findings.reader_payoff: The warning becomes an embodied act of protection meeting resistance, rather than only a statement about danger.
findings.containment: This is a surprising attributed analogy, not the lexical translation of luddan or tundhira, and no actual medicine is being claimed. The driving in 19:86 may describe an outcome without exerting pressure on the focus audience.

epistemic.reason: The focus and context coordinates match the HFT trace, and the ludd branch has an exact supplied oral-dose facet; the transfer from warning to dose remains an exploratory analogy from a legacy_unbound source.
